description: Publish-stage script that builds an offline QA web page for a set of NIfTI volumes with NiiVue's save-html extension. Each volume becomes a self-contained HTML scene holding the volume and NiiVue, so the page opens from disk with no server or network. One volume makes index.html that scene; several make one scene per volume plus an index.html that lists them beside a viewer showing one at a time.

volumes.description: Volumes to render into the QA page (typically the filtered volumes).

title.description: Heading shown on the QA page.

max_embed_mb.description: Largest volume, in MiB of image data, embedded at full resolution (at most 360); larger ones are embedded as a block-averaged preview at 1/2, 1/3, ... resolution that fits, and the page says so.

qa_html.description: Offline NiiVue QA web page (index.html); with several volumes, it lists the per-volume scene files written beside it and shows one at a time.

block.label: NiiVue QA Page
block.description: Render a shareable QA page with NiiVue saveHTML.

neuroflow/launch.description: Reads $NEUROFLOW_SESSION/context.json, loads each of inputs.volumes into a headless NiiVue, and writes its scene with generateHTML into $NEUROFLOW_OUTPUT_DIR. The standalone NiiVue bundle the scenes embed is built with esbuild on first use and cached in node_modules/.cache/neuroflow. If the extension can't be used, it writes a page that loads NiiVue from esm.sh beside copies of the volumes, and says so on stderr.

useWhen: Publish a web page that shows a set of volumes in NiiVue for quality review.
Share results with someone who only has a browser.

avoidWhen.when: A person should review and record corrections interactively.

preconditions: Each scene embeds its volume, so the page grows with the input. With many or high-resolution volumes, if the user has not said what they need, ask: fewer volumes, smaller previews (max_embed_mb), or full resolution.
effects: Writes index.html, plus one scene file per volume when there are several, to the output directory.
Each scene embeds its volume and NiiVue (about 4.5 MB of script), so the page works offline but is large.
If the save-html extension, NiiVue or esbuild is missing (run npm install), it warns on stderr and writes a page that loads NiiVue from esm.sh, which needs network access.

failures.meaning: The QA page could not be built.
failures.remedy: Read the error that follows in the step log; usually an input volume is missing.
